working_title: Social Security Paid Her by Mistake for Years. Then It Wanted $60,175.90 Back.
one_line: The Social Security Administration overpays millions of people because of its own errors, then demands every dollar back years later -- and until 2024 its default was to withhold the entire monthly cheque until the debt was cleared.
contradiction: She did nothing wrong, the government made the mistake, the government kept paying her anyway -- and the government's remedy was to take her whole income until a five-figure debt she never incurred was repaid.
scored_by: claude, 2026-08-12, v002 rubric, for the 45-minute slot

justification.personal_relevance: Seventy-seven per cent of this channel's measured audience is 55 or older. Social Security is not a system they might one day meet; it is the system that pays them this month. Maximum, and it is the highest-relevance premise on the slate for THIS audience.
justification.wtf_factor: 'The government's own error, and it takes your entire cheque' is a real 'that is allowed?'. Held under 15 because most viewers half-suspect it already; it confirms a fear rather than inverting an expectation.
justification.human_stakes: Income, housing and independence for people with no capacity to earn it back. Below the 43-years and lost-home tier, above two nights in a car. 12.
justification.contradiction: Paid yet still owing -- one of the four canonical contradictions named in the rubric itself. Maximum.
justification.story_arc: The weakest axis and the reason this is not ranked first. No single named person with a documented beginning-to-end arc has been retrieved: Justina Worrell is one figure and one letter, and her aunt speaks for her. Without a protagonist followed end to end this is 7, and 7 is exactly what sank EP70.
justification.title_power: The figure is the title. $60,175.90 is the kind of number the rubric's own example ($86,900) is built on. 9.
justification.thumbnail_power: One government letter, one number. That is the v002 evidence-thumbnail direction exactly. 9.
justification.evidence: Strong journalism (KFF Health News / Cox Media Group, internal SSA documents obtained, congressional testimony) but no court record and no docket. Documentary evidence rather than adjudicated evidence. 8.
justification.broad_audience: Everyone has a parent on Social Security even if they are not on it. 9.
justification.franchiseability: VA overpayments, Medicaid clawbacks, state unemployment clawbacks, student-aid recovery -- the same shape repeats across agencies. 5.
justification.evergreen: The policy moved in 2024 and moved back in 2025. Current, which buys attention now and dates the film later. 4.
justification.specific_money_amount: $60,175.90 demanded from Justina Worrell (KFF Health News, Overpayment Outrage series).
justification.major_reversal: In March 2024 the agency stopped withholding 100% of monthly cheques and defaulted to 10%; under the following administration full withholding resumed.
